name: PARK Rooftop Bar
seoTitle: PARK Lisboa: Car-Park Rooftop Drinks West of Chiado
tagline: A bar on the roof of a car park on Calçada do Combro, looking west over Bica to the river and the 25 de Abril Bridge

description.short: PARK is a bar on the top floor of a multi-storey car park at Calçada do Combro 58, between Bairro Alto and Bica. The terrace looks west over the rooftops to the Tagus and the 25 de Abril Bridge. It opens at 15:00 from Monday to Saturday and at noon on Sundays, and takes no reservations.
description.full:
PARK is an afternoon and evening place, and its opening hours decide whether it works on a port day. According to its official Instagram profile it opens from 15:00 to 02:00 Monday to Saturday and from 12:00 to 20:00 on Sundays, when it runs a 'Picnic' brunch session. Many day calls set all-aboard in the late afternoon, so on a weekday you may only get 45 minutes to an hour on the terrace before a 10-minute taxi back to the terminal. Sunday is the easiest day for a day-call visit.

The sunset drink it is known for only fits if your ship sails late or stays overnight, or in winter, when the sun sets around 17:15 to 18:30. The terrace faces west, so evening light falls straight across it. It does not take reservations, and on summer evenings the best seats along the edge go well before sunset.

From the ship it is about 2.2 km and 34 minutes on foot, finishing uphill. The simpler route is to walk 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia, take the metro Blue Line to Baixa-Chiado, leave by the Chiado exit, cross Largo do Camões and walk a few minutes west along Calçada do Combro. A taxi takes about 10 minutes.

The entrance is the car-park entrance itself, with no obvious sign at street level; go in and take the lift to the top. Upstairs there is an open terrace with plants and wooden seating, an indoor bar for cooler weather and a short food menu. DJs play from the evening, and the crowd gets younger and louder after dark.

Skip it if you have less than an hour to spare: the view is good but not unique, and São Pedro de Alcântara, ten minutes away, is free.
description.history: PARK opened in the early 2010s (2013 is the date usually given) on the roof of a working multi-storey car park on Calçada do Combro, a street that runs from Chiado towards São Bento along the edge of Bairro Alto and Bica. The idea of putting a bar on an unused car-park roof was new in Lisbon at the time, and it was among the first of the rooftop bars that have since opened across the city. The car park below still operates, which is why the entrance is easy to miss. Its 'PARKBEAT' DJ evenings and Sunday sessions have become regular fixtures.
description.significance: PARK is a good example of how Lisbon has reused awkward urban spaces: an ordinary concrete car park that gives one of the clearest west-facing views in the centre. For a cruise passenger, it is mainly useful as the closest relaxed rooftop to Chiado for a late-afternoon drink, provided the opening times fit the ship's schedule.

directions.general: Located on the 6th floor of a parking garage on Calçada do Combro, between Chiado and Bica
directions.fromCruisePort: About 2.2 km and 34 minutes on foot, finishing uphill. Taxi about 10 minutes; the bar is on top of a car park on Calçada do Combro, between Chiado and Bica.
directions.publicTransport: Metro: Baixa-Chiado station (Green/Blue lines), Chiado exit, then a short walk along Calçada do Combro. Tram 28 stops nearby. Bus routes 758, 773 to Bairro Alto.
directions.parking: The bar is IN a parking garage - park on lower floors and take elevator to 6th floor

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily; afternoons and evenings Monday to Saturday, daytime only on Sundays

seasonal.notes: Hours from PARK's official Instagram profile (@parklisboa). DJs in the evening.

admissionPrices.notes: Free entry, no reservations. Drinks roughly €5–12 (no current official menu is published online, so treat this as a guide).

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: From the 15:00 opening on a weekday, or Sunday from noon, if you are on a day call. For sunset on an overnight or late-departure call, arrive about an hour before sunset to get a seat.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Go in through the car-park entrance at Calçada do Combro 58 and take the lift to the top. There are no reservations. Bring a layer for the evening, when the terrace can be windy.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2 hours: 25–34 minutes each way plus 45 minutes to an hour on the terrace
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: The metro to Baixa-Chiado and a short, fairly level walk along Calçada do Combro avoid most of the climb from the river. A lift goes up through the car park; phone ahead if steps on the terrace are a concern.
combinableWith: Cais do Sodré and Pink Street (downhill)
tips: Check the day: it opens at 15:00 Monday to Saturday and at 12:00 on Sundays, so Sunday is the easiest day to fit in on a day call.
Work back from all-aboard time: allow about 10 minutes by taxi, or 34 minutes on foot, to the terminal.
Look for the car-park entrance at Calçada do Combro 58; there is no bar frontage at street level.
There are no reservations, so for sunset on a late-departure or overnight call arrive about an hour early.
The terrace faces west towards the river and the 25 de Abril Bridge; light is best late in the day.
From Baixa-Chiado metro (Chiado exit), cross Largo do Camões and walk a few minutes west along Calçada do Combro.
Bring a jacket for the evening; the roof is exposed to the wind off the river.

highlights: West-facing terrace over Bica and Santa Catarina to the Tagus
View of the 25 de Abril Bridge and the south bank
Planted rooftop on top of a working car park
DJs in the evenings and on Sunday afternoons
No reservations: first come, first served
facilities: Bar bites and light meals available

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Elevator access to 6th floor from parking garage. Once on rooftop level, relatively flat with some steps. The biggest challenge is reaching Bairro Alto district itself (steep hills).
